title: capability-ux.v1
description: Presentation and anchoring for one capability's input and outcome dialogs. It chooses among compatible presentations; it cannot widen a contract, invent a successful outcome, or make a system-owned field editable. Shape comes from the pinned input contract; permission comes from the input ownership declaration; only presentation comes from here.

subject.description: The published capability subject. Never a namespace or endpoint; the server resolves those.

pins.description: What this declaration was compiled against. A pin that no longer matches must produce a stale-publication finding before the experience is offered for execution.

groups.description: Presentation grouping over field pointers. Grouping and order are presentation; they never change which pointers exist or who owns them.

exampleSelector.description: For capabilities whose input is a retained fixture the server owns entirely. The user selects an example; the payload stays server-owned.

outcomes.description: One entry per permitted outcome contract and variant. A variant is matched by validated contract identity and discriminator, never guessed from which fields happen to be present.

match.description: How this variant is identified. contractId must match; a discriminator pointer narrows further.

isNegative.description: True for a declared negative domain outcome. A negative outcome has a declared layout of its own; it is never rendered as a success card.

delivery.description: How refused, uncertain and unmapped deliveries are presented. These are workbench delivery states, never fabricated capability output.

motion.description: Declared intents only. Duration and easing come from the shared presentation profile, and the animation never schedules execution or manufactures progress.

anchor.description: Where this dialog emerges from on the circuit. The semantic identity is authoritative; the graph entity id is a projection identifier that a re-layout may change.

nodeIdentity.description: Source identity of the anchoring node. Resolved against the scene at open time.

fallback.description: Used when the anchor node is not present in the current view. The dialog still carries its semantic identity.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the input contract. Must exist in the pinned schema and must be declared editable by the ownership declaration.

control.description: Preferred control. The registry decides whether it is compatible with the resolved schema shape; an incompatible preference is a compilation finding, not a silent substitution.

visibleWhen.description: Conditional presentation. It never bypasses required-field validation.

family.description: A registered outcome presentation family. A chart or artifact family is not offered until its component and bindings are established.

pointers.description: Named pointers a family requires, such as amount, currency, unit and timestamp for a metric.

dispositionLabels.description: Declared mapping from domain disposition to label. Provider success and business success stay separate.
